blind_spots.blind_spot: 'NDAA Compliant System' covers supply-chain component compliance, but the 'Smart AI Software' mission-planning platform has no mention of RMF/ATO/IL4-5 for the software layer if it ever touches a government network.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Passing NDAA on camera/radio components doesn't get the mission-planning software an ATO — a program office will ask about the software accreditation path separately, and that path isn't visible anywhere in public materials.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Compliance messaging is built around hardware supply-chain provenance (a well-understood box to check) rather than software-side government-network accreditation, which is a newer and less standardized ask.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Product is sold direct-to-checkout at fixed price points ($14,990 / $49,990 / $83,990) with a 'Get started' button — no description of prime/flow-down mechanics for integrating as a subcontractor on a program of record.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A DoD acquisition rarely buys off a public price list; a unit purchased this way outside a contract vehicle or prime relationship can stall the moment a program office needs FAR-compliant procurement, GFE integration, or a subcontract structure.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Commercial e-commerce motion (agriculture, public safety, inspection buyers) is the company's primary revenue engine, and the DoD-specific acquisition pathway hasn't been separately built out in public messaging.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: $83,990 Ultimate Multi-Mission Smart Plane. ... Get started

blind_spots.blind_spot: Three concurrent Army/Air Force SBIR Phase I/II efforts are running on a small team with no visible mention of an advocacy champion above the operator/pilot level to convert any one of them into a transition before funded months run out.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Operators loving the backpack-deployable plane at a demo is not the same as a program office committing budget past Phase II — with three SBIR clocks running at once, a single missed transition on a $5-10M-scale company is existential.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: SBIR abstract language (truncated in pack) focuses on the technical capability of the system, not on named transition partners or a program-of-record path.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: What if an airplane could fit within a rucksack, deploy in less than two minutes, fly for hours, and automatically detect threats in real time? Now it can with the highly capable and easy to use WingXpand™ small unmanned aerial system (sUAS)

opener_hook: WingXpand is running three concurrent Army/Air Force SBIR efforts on a roughly 15-person team — worth comparing funded months remaining against time-to-transition on each.
what_they_do: Backpack-portable fixed-wing/eVTOL sUAS with onboard edge-AI detection, sold to defense, agriculture, public safety, and infrastructure-inspection customers.
